rule: Use a native Foundryborne/Foundry document whenever one exists. Do not create a parallel type.

entities.notes: Native class Item; domains, linked class Items/features, inventory choices and character guide fields exist.
Native subclass Item with linkedClass, spellcastingTrait, featureState and linked features.
Native generic feature Item exists and is used by classes, subclasses, ancestries, adversaries and environments.
Domain itself is not an Item document type. Built-in domains are config entries; homebrew domains are merged from Foundryborne Homebrew settings.
Native Domain Card with domain, level, recallCost, card type, vault/loadout state, actions and resource support.
Native ancestry Item with linked features and optional loreReference.
Native community Item with linked feature UUIDs and optional loreReference.
Native inventory Item with tier, equip/secondary/burden, attack action, weapon features, actions and item resource.
Native inventory Item with tier, armor slots, thresholds, armor features, actions and item resource.
Native inventory Item, actions supported, consumeOnUse flag.
Native inventory Item with description and actions.
Generic SRD items should normally land in loot unless their mechanics make them a consumable/weapon/armor.
Native Beastform Item with tier, token data, trait, advantages, linked features and evolved/hybrid data.
Native adversary Actor with tier, adversary role/type, motives/tactics, difficulty, thresholds, attack, experiences and embedded feature Items.
Native environment Actor with tier, type, impulses, difficulty, potential adversaries, notes and embedded feature Items.
Foundryborne 2.7.2 documentTypes expose no transformation Item/Actor type. Keep neutral data; decide later between Journal + native effects/features or a small extension after an empirical pilot.
No dedicated Foundryborne document type; use one JournalEntry per Campaign Frame with pages and @UUID links.
Document the mechanic first. Promote only concrete roll tables/items/macros/actions when the rule benefits from automation.
Foundryborne already declares a RollTable compendium; use Foundry core RollTables.
Foundryborne declares a JournalEntry compendium; ancestry/community already support loreReference links.

important_findings: Environment is a native Actor, not a Journal.
Campaign Frame has no dedicated Foundryborne type and should be a JournalEntry.
Domain is configuration rather than a document type; Domain Cards are native Items.
Transformation has no native document type in Foundryborne 2.7.2.
Weapon already supports actions, features and a resource, which is a useful base for later evolving weapons.
Domain Card currently enforces character-domain membership on creation, so narrative Hunt cards will require a deliberately small extension later rather than a parallel card system.
